clue.text: Irony perfect somehow in Pericles

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of irony perfect are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A reader spots something perfectly ironic in Shakespeare's play Pericles.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's play is titled 'Pericles, Prince of Tyre', so the second half of the title stands for its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles is the hero of the Shakespeare play, whose title gives him this royal rank and city.

clue.text: Old lizard Mauro's content after pint with love

indicators.note: after places the middle of the name behind the pint and the love

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside it, so the name loses its outer letters

parts.note: the name Mauro

explanation.surface: Someone named Mauro owns a fossil lizard, apparently pickled after a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happiness but means the inside of a word; the 's on Mauro is only possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A pterosaur is an extinct flying reptile of the dinosaur age, loosely called an old lizard.

clue.text: Still at the crease: no boundaries in Perth

parts.note: a batsman at the crease is in, batting, in cricket

indicators.note: boundaries are the edges of the word, so Perth loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the Australian city

explanation.surface: A cricketer stands motionless at the crease, unable to hit any fours in a match in Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field; here the boundaries are the end letters of Perth.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, without movement, which is what still means as an adjective.

clue.text: Learner driver in vehicle with a woman

indicators.note: in puts the learner inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the learner plate shown by a learner driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A learner sits in a car with a female instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Mum, not married, sensible apart from that

indicators.note: not tells us the married letter is removed from the mother

parts.note: mum is a mother
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: Mum is unmarried, but in every other respect she is sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise is an adverb meaning in other respects or except for that.

clue.text: Spooner's dog — pointer — makes farewell

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped, after Rev Spooner

parts.note: a poodle is a breed of dog
a tip is a pointer, a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A pointer, a gun dog, signals a goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: A pointer is also a breed of dog, which makes the surface read as two dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is old-fashioned British slang for goodbye.

clue.text: River's river with carp, not wide

indicators.note: not removes the letter for wide

parts.note: to carp is to complain, to whine
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A river is home to carp, though it is not a wide one.
explanation.walkthrough: Carp looks like the fish but is the verb meaning to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a major European river flowing from the Alps to the North Sea.

clue.text: Displeased with department's representative sample

parts.note: cross means annoyed or displeased
a section is a department of an organisation

explanation.surface: An annoyed person is sent by their department as its representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a sample taken to be typical of a whole population.

clue.text: Magistrate of past and of future events

indicators.note: of here means drawn out of, so the letters are taken from inside the words future events

explanation.surface: A judge has jurisdiction over what has happened and what is still to come.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join of 'future events'; 'past and' reads as part of the surface, while 'Magistrate of past' defines a historical official.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a historical chief officer of a town or district in England who acted as a local magistrate.

clue.text: Smitten peri had to love goddess

indicators.note: smitten means struck hard, so the letters of peri had to are knocked about

explanation.surface: A fairy, struck with love, was compelled to adore a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: A peri is a fairy of Persian legend; smitten reads as being in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek deity of love and beauty.

clue.text: Marine mammal and mammoth, perhaps close up

parts.note: the mammoth was a kind of elephant, an example the perhaps signals
to seal is to close up

explanation.surface: A sea creature and a mammoth come close together.
explanation.definitionFit: The elephant seal is a huge seal of the ocean, named for the male's trunk-like nose.

clue.text: Song of no great length about husband's cat

indicators.note: about wraps the brief song around the husband's letter

parts.note: short means of no great length
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A short ditty is sung about a man's pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The shorthair is a breed of domestic feline, such as the British Shorthair.

clue.text: Loyal vassal in Belgian city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., a feudal subject bound to serve a lord
second meaning: the French-speaking city on the river Meuse in eastern Belgium

explanation.walkthrough: The word is spelt without its accent in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege man owed loyal service to his lord, and Liège is a city on the river Meuse.

clue.text: Sort of western pie that's cooked, good to be consumed

indicators.note: the anagram consumes, takes in, the good letter
cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters of pie that's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the pie is baked, with something good eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: A spaghetti western is a cowboy film made by Italian directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti westerns were a genre of Italian-made cowboy films from the 1960s.

clue.text: Sit and cry — he's suffering these?

definitions.text: Sit and cry — he's suffering these?

indicators.note: suffering suggests the words sit, cry and he's are in distress and so jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who sits sobbing is having a fit of emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterics are a fit of uncontrollable laughing or crying, which is what the person in the clue is suffering.

clue.text: Conductor's constipation appalling — pot not needed

indicators.note: appalling suggests something dreadful, a sign the letters are rearranged
not needed says the letters of pot are taken from the pool

explanation.surface: A conductor's constipation is so dreadful that a chamber pot will not help.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P, O and T out of CONSTIPATION and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Walk to embrace cold spell

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the walk goes around the cold letter

parts.note: a path is a walk

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a walk to meet a period of cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a period of time, as in a bad patch, much like a spell.

clue.text: Choose to study organ: be encouraged

parts.note: to take a subject is to choose to study it
the heart is an organ

explanation.surface: A student picks anatomy and gains confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is an idiom for gaining courage or confidence.

clue.text: Sound of my army band?

indicators.note: sound of says the answer is spoken the same as the word for my

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

explanation.surface: Someone hears a military band and exclaims at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of the answer are silent, so it is said like the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is a body of troops, a band of soldiers in an army.

clue.text: Coat's second layer worn by 'umble character

indicators.note: worn by puts the layer on, after, the character

parts.note: Uriah Heep in Dickens's David Copperfield keeps saying he is 'umble
skin is an outer layer

explanation.surface: A Dickens character wears a second layer of coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield who drops his h in 'umble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a coat made from the fleece-covered hide of a sheep.

clue.text: Your compiler's Conservative, not Liberal, making charge

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I'm

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the Liberal letter

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: The setter declares a political allegiance, Tory rather than Liberal, which is quite a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to fill or permeate, as to charge something with feeling.

clue.text: Sir Toby's noisy expulsion after dinner?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the surname of Sir Toby, the drunken knight in Twelfth Night
second meaning: a noisy release of gas from the stomach

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Toby Belch is the drunken knight of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, apt for the burp.
explanation.definitionFit: A belch is a burp, and Belch is Sir Toby's surname in the Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: Stops one throw being returned in cricket series

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the series

parts.note: the Ashes is the Test series between England and Australia

indicators.note: being returned means the one and the throw are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to lob is to throw high

explanation.surface: A fielder's single throw back in an Ashes match halts play.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to put a stop to something, so abolishes means stops.

clue.text: Bond I'd play regularly in unusual fashion

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of Bond I'd play is taken

explanation.surface: An actor says they would play James Bond in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddly is an adverb meaning strangely or in a peculiar manner.

clue.text: Cool to check out music genre

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
to check out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A trendy invitation to listen to a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is a style of rock and pop originally from independent record labels.

clue.text: Invalid filled in forms when touring university

indicators.note: touring goes round, so the anagram surrounds the university letter
forms means shapes, so the letters of filled in take a new shape

explanation.surface: A disabled student fills in paperwork while visiting a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person, but is the adjective meaning void.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nullified has been made void, so it is no longer valid.

clue.text: Crisis where District Attorney takes stuff in …

indicators.note: takes, with in, means the attorney takes the stuffing inside
in completes takes in, wrapping the attorney around the stuffing

parts.note: DA is the US abbreviation for District Attorney
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A legal crisis where a prosecutor admits evidence, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or tense event, a crisis.

clue.text: … this was used to prevent it!

definitions.text: … this was used to prevent it!

parts.words: … this was used to prevent it!
parts.note: read on from the previous clue, 'it' is someone taking stuff in, so a device to stop sex is meant

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 26-across, so 'it' is the District Attorney taking stuff in, read saucily.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval locking garment was supposedly worn by women to stop sexual intercourse.
